clue.text: The place to be chivvying the waiters?

indicators.note: chivvying means harrying and hustling, so the letters of the next two words are pushed about into a new order

explanation.surface: A diner fancies the trendiest spot is one where you hurry the staff along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chivvying the waiters' reads as a scene in a restaurant, but it rearranges THE WAITERS.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for the most fashionable or exciting spot, the centre of the action.

clue.text: Doctor sea air, restricting pressure in target area

indicators.note: restricting means holding in, so the sea air surrounds the pressure letter

parts.note: ozone is the popular name for bracing seaside air
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A medic treating the sea breeze, oddly mixed with talk of a target zone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like an instruction to rearrange, but here it is simply DR.
explanation.definitionFit: A designated area where paratroops or supplies are dropped is the target ground for the drop.

clue.text: Lethal tablet swallowed by father only half dissolved

indicators.note: swallowed by means taken inside, so the tablet goes into the word for father

parts.note: dad is an informal word for father
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet

indicators.note: half of the word only melts away, leaving its second half

explanation.surface: A pill gulped down by a parent but only partly dissolved sounds dangerous.
explanation.walkthrough: E is crossword shorthand for an ecstasy tablet.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something able to cause death, so they are close synonyms.

clue.text: Lodge close to dangerous river

indicators.note: close to means the end of the next word supplies its final letter

parts.note: the Tay is Scotland's longest river

explanation.surface: A cabin standing perilously near a hazardous river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lodge' looks like a noun, but here it is the verb to put up somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: To lodge somewhere is to reside there temporarily as a guest or boarder.

clue.text: Mad appeals about part of anatomy

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Crazy pleas concerning some bodily part, perhaps from a hypochondriac.
explanation.definitionFit: The throat prominence formed by the thyroid cartilage is a familiar feature of the human body.

clue.text: Crack car, it's said every boxer needs one

indicators.note: it's said means the words are spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: crack means expert, a pro, and a car is a motor

explanation.surface: Someone claims every fighter needs a top-class vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crack' looks like a verb, but it is the adjective for top-class.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxing bout has to be organised and financed by someone who stages and sells the fight.

clue.text: Judge's premium reduced out of hand

indicators.note: out of hand means uncontrolled, so the remaining letters run wild into a new order
reduced means cut short, so the last letter of the word is lopped off

explanation.surface: A magistrate's insurance payment cut and gone haywire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' drops the final M of PREMIUM; 'out of hand' rearranges PREMIU.
explanation.definitionFit: An official who rules on play in cricket or tennis acts as the arbiter of the game.

clue.text: Beastly noise as rhino and alligator both cleared out

indicators.note: each of the two animal names is emptied of its insides, leaving its outside letters

explanation.surface: A noisy animal din as a rhino and an alligator are both chased away.
explanation.definitionFit: The loud deep cry of a lion or similar creature is a sound made by a beast.

clue.text: Raced without underwear, got in at end of the season

definitions.text: got in at end of the season

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the racing word wraps around the garment

parts.note: hared means ran very fast
a vest is an undershirt in British usage

explanation.surface: Someone streaked without their underwear at the end of the season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking. In Britain a VEST is an undershirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Crops are gathered in at the close of the growing season, which is what bringing in a harvest means.

clue.text: In poem, Orpheus's rejected lover

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the concealed letters read backwards
in means the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: In a poem, the mythical singer Orpheus spurns a suitor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns OEMOR, hidden in 'poem, Orpheus', backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's young hero gives his name to any ardent wooer, so it is a byword for a passionate suitor.

clue.text: Knock in vain with dispatch

parts.note: a rap is a sharp knock
idly can mean to no purpose, fruitlessly

explanation.surface: Someone knocks fruitlessly while delivering a message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dispatch' suggests a message, but here it means speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something with dispatch means doing it with speed and promptness.

clue.text: Less fashionable silent model losing heart

parts.note: keeping mum means staying silent

indicators.note: losing heart means the middle letters of the word for model drop out

parts.note: a sitter poses for an artist

explanation.surface: A quiet catwalk model looking dowdier as she becomes dispirited.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing heart' removes the middle TT from SITTER.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dowdy and unstylish, like the stereotype of a middle-aged parent, makes something less chic.

clue.text: Part of satire unfair on youngster's clothing

indicators.note: clothing means the words wrap around and cover the answer within them

explanation.surface: A satirical piece complains about how children are dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying the opposite of what is meant is a key tool of the satirist.

clue.text: PM's country house accurately placed on map

parts.note: to chart is to plot something on a map
well can mean properly or correctly

explanation.surface: A prime minister's rural residence is precisely marked on the map.
explanation.walkthrough: CHARTWELL in Kent was Winston Churchill's country home.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kent estate was the family home of Winston Churchill, the wartime prime minister.

clue.text: Sound of repetitive music boosts artillery attacks

indicators.note: sound of tells us the words are heard, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: a canon is music in which a melody is repeated by overlapping voices, and aids means boosts

explanation.surface: Repetitive music's noise is said to encourage heavy bombardment.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy continuous gunfire from big guns is a sustained bombardment by artillery.

clue.text: Superiority of policies adopted by cricket ground

indicators.note: adopted by means taken in, so the policies go inside the ground

parts.note: Lord's is the famous London cricket ground
lines can mean policies, as in a party line

explanation.surface: A famous cricket club's policies betray an air of superiority.
explanation.walkthrough: LORD'S is the London cricket ground known as the home of cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Haughty arrogance and a grand manner, like that of a noble, are a kind of superiority.

clue.text: Idle business associate one often has relations with?

definitions.meaning: an investor in a firm who takes no active part in running it
taken literally, the person who shares one's bed, with whom one has sexual relations

explanation.surface: A lazy colleague, then a nudge about who one is intimate with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relations' looks like family, but the second reading is about bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A silent investor in a firm, and literally the person one sleeps beside.

clue.text: Two pounds included in bill for sampler

indicators.note: included in means put inside the next word

parts.note: a bill is a poster stuck on a wall
L is the abbreviation for a pound, so two are LL

explanation.surface: A shopping bill showing two pounds for an embroidered sampler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bill' looks like an invoice but here is a poster.
explanation.definitionFit: An opinion surveyor tests a sample of the population to gauge its views.

clue.text: Treatment for a lunatic at sea?

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase, matching the adjective

indicators.note: treatment means the letters are handled and reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A cure for madness might be a sea voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' suggests confusion, but the definition means maritime.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to ships and sailing means belonging to the sea.

clue.text: Free performance gents ultimately appreciate?

parts.note: a turn is a stage act or performance
loos are lavatories, and the gents is a men's toilet

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the final letter is taken

explanation.surface: A free show at which gents eventually show their appreciation.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the 'gents' is a men's public toilet, and LOO is a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: To let something go or release it from restraint is to set it free.

clue.text: Queen turned up days before royal agents, historically

indicators.note: turned up in a down clue means read from bottom to top

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the usual abbreviation for the queen
an eve is the day before a festival or event

explanation.surface: The monarch showed up a few days ahead of her courtiers.
explanation.walkthrough: A reeve was a medieval official managing an estate or district for the king or lord.
explanation.definitionFit: In medieval England these were officials, such as shire reeves, acting for the crown.

clue.text: Singular act of slaughter leads to row

parts.note: S is the grammar abbreviation for singular
a cull is a selective killing of animals

explanation.surface: One mass killing sparks a quarrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like a quarrel, but it means to propel a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: To propel a boat with oars is to row it.

clue.text: In the end, chefs use identical seeds for flavouring

indicators.note: in the end means only the final letter of each of the next two words is taken

parts.note: same means identical

explanation.surface: Cooks ultimately all reach for the same seeds to add taste.
explanation.definitionFit: The small oily seeds of this plant are used to flavour bread and other dishes.

clue.text: Flower releases its aroma in minimal amounts

parts.note: frees means releases

indicators.note: minimal amounts means only the very first letter of each of the next two words

explanation.surface: A bloom gives off only a faint scent.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragrant flowering plant from South Africa, popular in bouquets, is a kind of bloom.

clue.text: Female facing malevolent charge

parts.note: ill can mean evil or malevolent, as in ill will

explanation.surface: A woman faces a spiteful accusation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' looks like an accusation, but it means to load.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge a container or weapon is to load it, which means to make it full.

clue.text: Defender of good French wine must be drunk

indicators.note: drunk means swallowed, so the wine is taken inside the French word

parts.note: bon is the French word for good
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine

explanation.surface: A champion of good French wine insists it be drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must be drunk' suggests a drinker, but means the French word takes the wine in.
explanation.definitionFit: A stronghold or a person who stoutly upholds a cause acts as its protector.

clue.text: Horned animal one passes with relief?

definitions.meaning: the thing handed on when people pass responsibility to someone else, glad to be rid of it

explanation.surface: An antlered beast, and something gratefully handed on.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'pass the buck' is to shift responsibility onto another person.
explanation.definitionFit: A male deer, and the token of responsibility in the idiom about passing it on.

clue.text: Vassal's gone on vacation in pursuit of romance

indicators.note: in pursuit of means following, so the emptied word comes after

parts.note: to romance is to tell fanciful untruths

indicators.note: on vacation means emptied, so only the outer letters of the word remain

explanation.surface: A servant has gone on holiday chasing love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'romance' looks like love, but here it means to tell tall tales.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically the word could name either party in a feudal bond, including the vassal who owed loyalty.

clue.text: Take in strange oxygen-depleted moonscapes

indicators.note: strange means odd, so the remaining letters form an unusual arrangement
oxygen is chemical symbol O, and depleted means one is taken away

explanation.surface: Absorbing weird lunar landscapes lacking any air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oxygen-depleted' removes one O from MOONSCAPES; 'strange' rearranges MONSCAPES.
explanation.definitionFit: To include or surround something within a scope is to embrace or comprise it.
